REFORMS
AND RESULTS
Three years ago, the World Bank Group launched its reform agenda
with a clear ambition: to become a faster, simpler, more effective,
and impactful institution — one better equipped to meet the scale and
urgency of today’s development challenges.
That agenda is now delivering results:
• Private capital mobilization
Public capital alone is not enough to tackle the world’s most pressing
development challenges. That’s why we mobilized $112 billion in private
funds in fiscal 2026 — more than triple the $35 billion mobilized in fiscal
2022 — to further expand opportunity, create jobs, and build infrastructure.
We also issued $25 billion in guarantees this year — surpassing our goal of
issuing $20 billion annually by 2030 — to give investors the confidence to
invest in developing countries.

BUDGET MANAGEMENT
In fiscal 2026, the World Bank Group evolved its budget
processes to enhance transparency and efficiency.
These reforms established a more integrated budget
framework across IFC, MIGA, and the World Bank,
linking business planning, workforce planning,
and budget decisions more directly to institutional
priorities and development outcomes. They simplified
planning and reporting processes, improved visibility
of total resources, and introduced stronger tools for
management oversight. The reforms also streamlined
cost-sharing arrangements, improved the treatment
of donor and external funding, reduced some clientfacing fees, and strengthened financial forecasting
and revenue visibility. They further supported financial
sustainability by creating efficiencies and redeploying
resources to fund strategic priorities.

In its second year, fiscal 2026, the World Bank Group
Guarantee Platform issued $17.9 billion in guarantees
to 110 projects in 32 countries, an increase of
46 percent over fiscal 2025. Of this, MIGA issued a
record $10.6 billion in new guarantees across 60

private investment to facilitate economic development

• Provide 300,000 people and businesses with

• Strengthen food and nutrition security for

• Enable 2.7 gigawatts in renewable energy capacity

WORLD BANK GROUP INITIATIVES
Our focus on job creation requires us to enhance our
external partnerships to generate new ideas. In fiscal
2026, the World Bank Group and partners launched a
new Mission 300 Private Sector Council to mobilize
the billions in private investment needed to connect
300 million Africans to electricity by 2030, and unlock
job creation across the continent. The Council,
comprising 14 leaders from diverse sectors, will help
drive strategies to accelerate commercial investment
that supports both energy access and employment.
Three years ago, the World Bank Group launched the
Private Sector Investment Lab to identify what was
holding back private investment in emerging markets.
Building on its work, we created the High-Level
Advisory Council on Jobs in 2024 to develop actionable
strategies for large-scale job creation. Both groups
brought together leaders from finance, business, and
government to provide new, outside-in thinking.

We are building a One World Bank Group client
coverage model that aligns public and private sector

Strategy. Guided by select solutions underpinned

Support will be differentiated to reflect individual
country contexts, while using regional approaches,

WORLD BANK GROUP INITIATIVES
Our focus on job creation requires us to enhance our
external partnerships to generate new ideas. In fiscal
2026, the World Bank Group and partners launched a
new Mission 300 Private Sector Council to mobilize
the billions in private investment needed to connect
300 million Africans to electricity by 2030, and unlock
job creation across the continent. The Council,
comprising 14 leaders from diverse sectors, will help
drive strategies to accelerate commercial investment
that supports both energy access and employment.
Three years ago, the World Bank Group launched the
Private Sector Investment Lab to identify what was
holding back private investment in emerging markets.
Building on its work, we created the High-Level
Advisory Council on Jobs in 2024 to develop actionable
strategies for large-scale job creation. Both groups
brought together leaders from finance, business, and
government to provide new, outside-in thinking.

In fiscal 2026, the World Bank Group launched the
fifth Managed Co-lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) for
credit insurers and signed a $6 billion credit insurance
policy — the largest mobilization in one agreement —
with 19 global insurance companies to support up to
$10 billion in new IFC lending to small- and mediumsized businesses in emerging markets. During the
fiscal year, IFC executed securitization transactions
across both funded (cash) and unfunded (synthetic)
structures, drawing on the expertise of banks that
acted as arrangers and/or distribution banks, and
attracted participation from institutional investors,
asset managers, banks, and insurance companies.
Commercial banks remained key syndications
partners, co-investing alongside the World Bank
Group in transactions. By leveraging the expertise,
capital, and market reach of private investors, the
World Bank Group increases financing available to
clients while promoting private sector-led growth.

Brazil’s family farms employ nearly 10 million people and play a central
role in food production. Our partnership with the government, launched
in fiscal 2026, aims to support 1 million family farms with improved
technology, market logistics, and insurance by 2030.
This partnership is part of the World Bank Group’s strategic priority
that aims to move 300 million farmers from subsistence to surplus.
Our three-pillar strategy leverages the World Bank Group’s unique
capabilities. First, the World Bank and IFC strengthen the foundations
of family farms by investing in physical and human capital, such as rural
roads and research. Then, they align regulations, streamline standards,
repurpose subsidies, and remove barriers to doing business. Finally,
the World Bank Group expands access to finance through MIGA’s
guarantees and insurance, as well as partnerships created by the
World Bank and IFC. The private sector is a critical partner across
all three pillars.

• Greater efficiency
Across the World Bank Group, we’ve consolidated country office leadership
and eliminated bureaucratic duplication, making it faster and easier for us to
address our clients’ priorities. We cut average project-approval times from
19 months to nine, with some low-risk projects approved in as little as 60 days.
• Corporate initiatives
We’re deploying AI to accelerate our work and working with partners to promote
AI solutions that are safe and impactful for everyone. We focus on practical
applications that solve everyday problems in developing countries.
• Clear outcomes
Our Scorecard now focuses on 22 key metrics that show how our work creates
jobs and improves lives. And our Target Map keeps us ambitious against 10
strategic priorities. We publish our data online, making it more user-friendly and
leading to better outcomes.
